reason.camera_poe_over: ⚠️ Estimated draw ({est} W) is CLOSE TO/ABOVE the {budget} W budget — check camera power.
reason.bt_upgrade: All-802.3bt model selected: {bt} need 802.3bt PoE to run every radio.
reason.core: Traffic aggregation: {n} at the access layer. The 10G core terminates all uplinks.
reason.core_redundant: Traffic aggregation: {n} at the access layer. {qty}× {model} in a stack/MC-LAG — N+1 core redundancy for a critical site (losing one does not take the network down).
reason.fw_switch_limit: FortiLink limit: manages up to {limit} switches (need {need}).
reason.fw_10g: Has 10G SFP+ ports for fibre uplinks.
reason.fw_throughput: Threat protection {tp} Gbps covers {need} Gbps of inspected traffic (~{pct}%).
reason.fw_none: {need} switches on site — above the limit of every listed model.
reason.fw_ha: HA pair (active-passive) — a single firewall is an unacceptable single point of failure for a critical site.
reason.ups_legacy: Estimated active equipment load ≈{w} W (excluding camera/AP PoE). Choose a UPS with ≥30% headroom and the runtime the site requires.
reason.ups: Load ≈{w} W: equipment {eq} W + PoE {poe} W (APs and cameras, incl. PSU efficiency). Needs ≥{va} VA with {head}% headroom. Confirm the required runtime.
reason.oob: Independent access path to the firewall/consoles if the main link fails — essential for remote recovery without a site visit.
reason.dac: Short 10G links within one rack (switches ↔ core ↔ FortiGate) — a DAC is cheaper and more reliable than a pair of optics.
reason.sr: Fibre uplinks between closets ({idf} closets/IDF): 2 transceivers per link.
reason.gc: {model} has no SFP+: switches connect with a 1G copper SFP into the FortiLink port.
reason.patch_panels: {n} copper ports (sockets, cameras, APs) ÷ {ports} ports per panel.
reason.patch_cords: One patch cord per used port.
reason.cable_managers: Horizontal cable managers for tidy patching.
reason.rack_idf: Extra racks for remote IDF closets: {n} (90 m copper limit).
reason.spare: {pct}% of {qty} pcs (minimum 1) — swap immediately instead of waiting for RMA at the “{tier}” level.
reason.management: FortiManager / FortiAnalyzer (or FortiGate Cloud) — central configuration management and log retention. FAZ size depends on log volume (GB/day).

help.html:
How SiteSizer sizes a location

Every input change instantly recalculates the BoM, diagram, IP plan and power. All numbers below come from the catalog — you can change them in “Catalog”.

1. Growth reserve

When enabled, sockets, cameras and access points (each zone separately) are multiplied by (1 + {reserve}%) and rounded up before switches are sized — so the reserve may add a switch.

2. Switches

    {cats}

Base or premium model. Premium models have two hot-swap power supplies. They are recommended for important sites (tiers 1–2), and the app asks you to confirm. If the APs need more 802.3bt PoE ports (FAP-241K, FAP-441K) than FS-124G-FPOE offers (8), FS-624F-FPOE (24 × 802.3bt) is selected automatically.

PoE. AP draw comes from datasheets, camera draw from the “Camera power draw” field (default {cam} W). A warning appears above {warn}% of the budget; if the budget is short, switches are added.

3. Core (aggregation)

“Auto” adds an FS-1024E when there are ≥ {agg} access switches. A core needs a FortiGate with 10G SFP+, so FG-80F is skipped. One FS-1024E has 24 × 10G ports: if more switches are needed, another core group is added and a warning is shown.

4. FortiGate

The first model in the ladder that passes every limit is chosen: FortiSwitch count, FortiAP count, 10G ports (with a core) and, if inspected traffic is given, threat-protection throughput with {head}% headroom.

{ladder}

5. Criticality tiers

{tiers}
TierAddsSLA

6. Power, rack, cabling

Power uses datasheet values plus the real PoE load including PSU efficiency. UPS with {ups}% headroom. The rack is sized from rack units (equipment, patch panels, managers, UPS) with spare space. Runs over 90 m need extra closets (IDF) with fibre uplinks.

Uplink oversubscription is calculated per category; ≤ {oversub}:1 is recommended.

7. IP plan

Each segment (Data, Voice, Wi-Fi, Guest, CCTV, IoT, Management) gets the smallest subnet that fits its devices + {buf}% + 2 reserved addresses. With a base network (e.g. 10.50.0.0/16) subnets are carved without overlaps, with a gateway (first address) and DHCP pool.

8. Checks

The checks panel shows three levels: error (will not work), warning (worth reviewing), note (good to know). Some have action buttons — e.g. confirming dual power supplies.

Keyboard

Tab next field, arrows ±1, Ctrl+K command palette, Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Y undo / redo, Ctrl+S save, Ctrl+E / Ctrl+P Excel / PDF.
